channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Dolphins QB Quinn Ewers suffered a groin injury in Friday’s preseason game against the Commanders.
item.description: The Dolphins signed QB Mark Gronowski after Ewers picked up the injury. Ewers is the Dolphins’ primary backup, so the team was a little short-staffed for the remaining preseason games. Dolphins backup OT Jamaree Salyer reportedly suffered a season-ending injury.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Jeremy McNichols (quad) will be sidelined a few weeks.
item.description: McNichols probably is no higher than fourth on the depth chart in Washington behind ‘Bill,’ Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen. Missing time due to injury doesn’t bode well for him making the initial 53-man roster.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Isaiah Likely is leading all first-team receivers in catches “by a wide margin.”
item.description: With Malik Nabers still off the field, that’s a given. Still, Likely finds himself as barely a top-12 tight end by ADP. The argument could be made that he belongs closer to the top 10. “Given the way [Jaxson] Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed,” Raanan concludes.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden believes Malik Benson has been the Raiders top performer at training camp and could overtake Jack Bech as Las Vegas’ third wideout.
item.description: Benson has been inundated with buzz this offseason. He caught two balls for 26 yards on four targets in Las Vegas’ first preseason game and reportedly has a strong connection with Fernando Mendoza. Outside of Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty it’s been hard to recommend any Raiders skill position player in fantasy circles this year; perhaps the sixth-round pick can step into a real target role given the lack of competition around him.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Packers EDGE Lukas Van Ness (shoulder) is not practicing on Sunday.
item.description: Severity is unknown at this point and the injury didn’t happen at the practice, so we’ll await further team comment before getting too worried. The Packers definitely can’t afford to have Van Ness down with Micah Parsons already on pace to miss the first month of the season.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco believes Parker Washington has “established himself” as the Jaguars’ WR1.
item.description: Washington has been Lawrence’s “favorite target, and he always seems to be open” DiRocco notes. The Jaguars main pass catchers are pretty close in ADP, with Washington leading the way at WR31 and Brian Thomas Jr. at WR33. This would seem to be an argument to trust Washington as a true WR2/WR3 option — and everything we’ve gotten on Washington this offseason from beat writers has been overwhelmingly positive.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Bears assistant head coach Antwaan Randle El called offensive plays in the second half of Chicago’s 34-10 win over the Browns in Week 1 of the preseason.
item.description: It certainly can’t hurt his case for head coaching work should the Bears offense continue to play well above the league average. Randle El’s offensive playcalling produced 235 yards and 24 points in the second half.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Marcus Mariota (knee) sprained his MCL and will miss the remainder of the preseason.
item.description: Frankly, a pretty good update considering how quickly Mariota exited the field on Friday. The Commanders will likely pick up another quarterback to help navigate the final two weeks of the preseason. Mariota will be the backup for the season opener if healthy.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-5 targets for 20 yards in Kansas City’s first preseason game.
item.description: The good news is that Allen worked with the starters in the slot. The bad news is that he worked well into the second half in the first preseason game while leading the team in targets. He’s clearly the highest-upside stash receiver of the group, but playing deep into the first preseason game isn’t a great sign for his chances of early playing time.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson was “one of the positives coming out of” their first preseason game.
item.description: Johnson had 12 carries for 59 yards and three catches for 10 yards against the Rams. While we’ve seen a little camp buzz about Johnson, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell presents this as a step forward for Johnson who “has been running with the fourth-string offense most of training camp.” He’s still probably the best back to have rostered in the event of a Kenneth Walker injury, but this isn’t such an important role that the backup necessarily needs to be rostered in standard redraft leagues.-Rivers McCown
